note: HAND-CURATED source of truth for the non-engine SDK surface: version constants, API-table shapes, game_ram accessors, public records, and context-tagged lifecycle callbacks. tools/sdk_gen.py turns it, together with functions.json, into sdk/include/roth_sdk.h, sdk/abi/descriptor.json, and the generated host support files.

version.load_rule: A plugin loads iff abi_major == host.abi_major AND abi_minor <= host.abi_minor. Additive growth requires a minor bump; a breaking change requires a major bump. The engine-call table's slot order is exposure order and is frozen ABI: new exposures append at the end, existing slot offsets never move, and the exposure-order gate enforces prefix stability against the released baseline. Version 0.8 appends the roth_interfaces_v1 host-service sub-table, the plugin-to-plugin interface registry. Version 0.7 adds the centered-engine-over-source-canvas composite mode and appends an optional engine-index baseline plane to roth_world_frame_v1. Version 0.6 appends the PRESENT context, the roth_present_v1 and roth_window_v1 host-service sub-tables, and the on_map_loaded, on_palette_changed, on_video_mode_changed, and on_present_pace callbacks. Version 0.5 appends blit_das_image_to_buffer and draw_popup_shadow_border_smc to the engine table. Version 0.4 appends game_ram->to_ptr, struct roth_mouse_poll_v1, the on_scancode and on_mouse_poll callbacks, and roth_api_v1->plugin_dir().

contexts.note: Platform-neutral execution contexts (design 10.4) — SDK LAW. Every callback is context-suffixed; restricted contexts get a restricted API view; functions reachable from TICK_ISR are non-overrideable in v1. Enumerators are FROZEN (ABI): never renumber.

values.name: ROTH_CTX_MAIN
values.desc: boot / main thread: discovery, validation, patching — all before the timer/game/audio threads start

values.name: ROTH_CTX_GAME
values.desc: game thread: per-frame logic; engine calls are legal here

values.name: ROTH_CTX_TICK_ISR
values.desc: timer-tick / compositor context: restricted API view, no engine calls

values.name: ROTH_CTX_AUDIO
values.desc: audio callback context: restricted API view

values.name: ROTH_CTX_PRESENT
values.desc: host present thread: runs once per host present-loop iteration (not per game tick or necessarily per physical refresh). No engine calls, game_ram writes, blocking, or frame submission; intended for pacing and coordination only

game_ram.note: Bounded little-endian accessors over game_ram (the contiguous engine global-state image at the 1996 layout; design 10.6). OFFSETS are canonical VAs = the frozen 1996 addresses (a permanent ABI). All reads/writes are bounds-checked against the game_ram size; out-of-range reads return 0, out-of-range writes are dropped, block ops return -1. Pointer-taxonomy + pool-lifetime rules (never cache a pool-derived pointer across an engine call/tick) live in sdk/README.md.

accessors.name: read_block
accessors.desc: copy n bytes from game_ram+off into dst; returns 0 on success, -1 if out of range

accessors.name: write_block
accessors.desc: copy n bytes from src into game_ram+off; returns 0 on success, -1 if out of range

accessors.name: size
accessors.desc: game_ram size in bytes (the bound for every accessor)

accessors.name: to_ptr
accessors.desc: resolve a canonical VA (game_ram offset) to its host pointer (base+off); NULL if out of range. The VA->host-pointer op: use it to form a game_ram pointer to pass to an exposed engine fn, or to match a stored runtime code/data pointer (which the engine writes as VA+base). Do NOT deref beyond the named global's extent; never cache across an engine call/tick.

mouse_poll.note: The SDK-neutral view of an int33 mouse-poll result, handed to on_mouse_poll (roth_on_mouse_poll_game_fn). Mirrors the host g_mods_int33_filter seam's (ax, regs) contract for the poll subfunctions: ax is the subfunction (read-only); ebx/ecx/edx are the result registers (in/out — a plugin may clear the low 16 bits to hide the mouse from the game, exactly as an overlay does while it captures input). GAME context, so engine calls are legal from the callback.

fields.name: ax
fields.desc: int33 subfunction (read-only): 3 = button+position status, 0xb = motion counters

fields.name: ebx
fields.desc: in/out: subfn 3 button state in the low bits (bit0=L, bit1=R); clear low16 to hide buttons from the game

fields.name: ecx
fields.desc: in/out: subfn 3 X position / subfn 0xb X motion counter (signed int16 in the low word)

fields.name: edx
fields.desc: in/out: subfn 3 Y position / subfn 0xb Y motion counter (signed int16 in the low word)

host_api.note: Host services on the top-level roth_api_v1 table beyond the engine/game_ram sub-tables (appended after game_ram; design 10). plugin_dir is loader-provided plugin identity: the directory of the plugin whose MAIN lifecycle callback (on_load / on_game_ram_ready / on_register_overrides / on_unload) is currently executing — i.e. mods/<name>/, the folder beside its plugin.so — so a plugin can locate its cfg/assets without knowing the game dir or its own name. Returns "" outside a MAIN dispatch (its value is only meaningful while a MAIN callback runs single-threaded at boot).

fields.name: plugin_dir
fields.desc: directory of the currently-dispatching plugin (valid during MAIN lifecycle callbacks; "" otherwise)

api_tables.note: Host-service sub-tables reached through trailing pointer fields of roth_api_v1. Each sub-table leads with struct_size so a plugin can feature-detect appended methods. Platform implementations bind through the generated host adapter table.

tables.field_desc: full-colour world-frame present channel (NULL on a host that predates it)
tables.note: The full-colour world present channel. submit_world_frame is GAME-context only and copies the described source before returning. The first plugin whose submission returns ROTH_OK owns the channel until unload; submissions and withdrawals from other plugins return ROTH_ERR_NOT_OWNER. The owner may withdraw immediately. If an owner stops submitting without withdrawing, the host stops compositing after 16 present iterations as a crash-safety backstop. Query get_present_caps instead of assuming dimension limits.

members.name: struct_size
members.desc: sizeof(struct roth_present_v1) as the host built it (feature-detect newer methods)

members.name: submit_world_frame
members.desc: copy and publish one caller-built frame descriptor. The viewport is required, travels with the frame, and is clipped to the current engine dimensions. Returns roth_result

members.name: withdraw_world_frame
members.desc: stop compositing the owner's world frame immediately; returns ROTH_ERR_NOT_OWNER for another plugin

members.name: get_present_caps
members.desc: write the host dimension limits and supported format bitmask; returns roth_result

tables.field_desc: window and display control, host-owned (NULL on a host that predates it)
tables.note: Window and display control. GAME-context setters validate and record requests; the host present thread applies them and publishes the applied state and result. A minimum present interval is post-present sleep and composes with synchronization, so the slower limit wins. Display modes are an informational snapshot of the window's current display for settings UIs; the host republishes the list when the window changes display. No mode-set operation is provided.

members.name: struct_size
members.desc: sizeof(struct roth_window_v1) as the host built it (feature-detect newer methods)

members.name: set_window_mode
members.desc: record a ROTH_WINMODE_* request. Exclusive fullscreen returns ROTH_ERR_UNSUPPORTED in this ABI version

members.name: set_present_mode
members.desc: record a ROTH_PRESENT_* request; adaptive mode may be rejected when applied

members.name: set_min_present_interval_us
members.desc: record the minimum host present interval in microseconds; zero is uncapped. To convert an fps setting, use 1000000 / fps

members.name: get_window_state
members.desc: copy the last applied window state; returns roth_result

members.name: get_display_mode_count
members.desc: number of modes in the informational current-display snapshot

members.name: get_display_mode
members.desc: read one snapshot entry; refresh is millihertz and output pointers may be NULL. Returns ROTH_ERR_RANGE for an invalid index

tables.field_desc: plugin-to-plugin interface registry (NULL on a host that predates it)
tables.note: The plugin-to-plugin interface registry. A plugin publishes a named, versioned pointer to a table it owns, and any other plugin looks it up by name; the host stores the name and the pointer and never interprets what the pointer leads to. The contract behind a name (the table layout, its calling contexts, what a version number means) belongs to the publisher, who documents it and ships a header for it. Names are reverse-DNS like plugin ids, and a breaking change takes a new name. publish, lookup and withdraw are MAIN or GAME context only. Every on_load completes before the first on_game_ram_ready, so a plugin that publishes in on_load is found by a lookup made from on_game_ram_ready or later, whatever the load order; a lookup for a name nobody has published returns NULL, and that is the ordinary answer when the publisher is not installed. The published table must stay valid until the publisher's on_unload returns, when the host withdraws whatever the plugin still has published. Plugins unload in reverse load order, so a consumer must not call through a looked-up interface from its own on_unload.

members.name: struct_size
members.desc: sizeof(struct roth_interfaces_v1) as the host built it (feature-detect newer methods)

members.name: publish
members.desc: publish iface under name (1 to 63 characters, containing a '.'; the host copies it). version is the publisher's own revision number for the table. Publishing a name the caller already holds replaces the pointer and version. Returns ROTH_ERR_NOT_OWNER when another plugin holds the name, ROTH_ERR_INVALID for a bad name or a NULL iface, and ROTH_ERR_NOMEM when the registry is full

members.name: lookup
members.desc: the pointer published under name, or NULL when nothing is. Writes the published version through version when it is not NULL and the name was found

members.name: withdraw
members.desc: stop offering name; later lookups return NULL. Returns ROTH_ERR_NOT_OWNER when another plugin holds the name and ROTH_ERR_INVALID when nothing is published under it

callbacks.note: Context-tagged lifecycle callback typedefs (design 10.4). v0.1 seed only — the loader milestone finalizes the plugin-query export, override callback typedefs (roth_next_<fn>), and the resolved-chain contract. Each takes the immutable host API table.

typedefs.name: roth_on_load_main_fn
typedefs.desc: plugin init, after validation, before any engine thread starts

typedefs.name: roth_on_game_ram_ready_main_fn
typedefs.desc: game_ram staged pristine and ready to patch, still pre-threads

typedefs.name: roth_on_frame_game_fn
typedefs.desc: per-frame hook on the game thread

typedefs.name: roth_on_compose_tick_isr_fn
typedefs.desc: compositor tick: draw onto the published 8-bit indexed frame (pixels[width*height]) — restricted API view, NO engine calls

typedefs.name: roth_on_register_overrides_main_fn
typedefs.desc: register function overrides: call roth_override(reg, ROTH_FN_<fn>, my_cb, priority) for each. Runs on MAIN after on_load, before any engine/timer/audio thread — the host builds the immutable priority chains and patches entries from these registrations

typedefs.name: roth_on_scancode_tick_isr_fn
typedefs.desc: input seam: every keystroke before the engine sees it, in TICK_ISR context (keyboard-ISR surrogate: NO engine calls). Return the (possibly rewritten) set-1 scancode, or 0 to SWALLOW the key (no state change, like a dropped prefix). Chained across plugins in load order; a 0 return stops the chain.

typedefs.name: roth_on_mouse_poll_game_fn
typedefs.desc: int33 mouse seam: fires on the GAME thread after each mouse poll (engine calls legal), with the SDK-neutral roth_mouse_poll_v1 result. Read mp->ax + the poll registers; modify ebx/ecx/edx to filter what the game sees (overlay input capture). Chained across plugins in load order.

typedefs.name: roth_on_map_loaded_game_fn
typedefs.desc: a new level's geometry, textures, and per-map colour tables are staged and ready to read. The first map event a plugin sees carries ROTH_EVENT_INITIAL.

typedefs.name: roth_on_palette_changed_game_fn
typedefs.desc: the VGA DAC palette changed. The synthetic first event carries ROTH_EVENT_INITIAL. Screen fades can produce a burst of events; heavy consumers may debounce.

typedefs.name: roth_on_video_mode_changed_fn
typedefs.desc: the engine pixel dimensions changed. The event also carries the logical aspect dimensions used by the host present path, and the synthetic first event carries ROTH_EVENT_INITIAL.

typedefs.name: roth_on_present_pace_fn
typedefs.desc: called exactly once per host present-loop iteration immediately before the host presents. alpha is (now - last_tick) / (last_tick - prev_tick), clamped to [0,1]; before two ticks exist it is 1. Interpolate lerp(snapshot[N-1], snapshot[N], alpha) for smooth tick-latent motion. No engine calls, game_ram writes, blocking, or frame submission.

overrides.note: The runtime function-override registration surface (task #103, MODS_PLATFORM.md §11.4). A plugin implements on_register_overrides(MAIN) and, inside it, calls roth_override(reg, ROTH_FN_<fn>, callback, priority) for each function it wants to wrap. `callback` has the GENERATED typed signature roth_override_<fn>_fn (in roth_sdk_overrides.h): (struct roth_chain *chain, const struct roth_api_v1 *api, <original args...>) -> <original ret>; it forwards to the next link (or the recorded original body) via roth_next_<fn>(chain, args...). The host builds one immutable, priority-sorted chain per function id (stable plugin-id tiebreak; duplicate priorities rejected in strict mode) and patches only functions with a non-empty chain, at boot, before any thread starts. Chain context is an invocation-local stack object (no TLS). Higher priority = OUTER (runs first). Registrar/chain structs are hand-curated here; the per-function typedefs + roth_next_<fn> thunks are generated from override_targets.json (eligible set) into roth_sdk_overrides.h.

registrar_fields.name: struct_size
registrar_fields.desc: sizeof(struct roth_registrar_v1) as the host built it (forward-compat sizing)

registrar_fields.name: override
registrar_fields.desc: record one override into fn_id's chain; returns 0 on success, non-0 if fn_id is not an eligible/present override target (the loader logs the reason). Prefer the roth_override() convenience wrapper.

plugin.note: The plugin-side contract (loader milestone, design 10.4 + review finding 16). A plugin is a shared object (mods/<name>/plugin.so) exporting exactly ONE versioned function, roth_plugin_query_v1(), returning a pointer to a static roth_plugin_info_v1. abi_major/abi_minor/struct_size lead the struct (design 10.5). The reverse-DNS id is the binary-authoritative plugin identity; a mod.toml beside the .so is packaging metadata ONLY (v1 ignores it). Load rule: the loader accepts the plugin iff abi_major == host.abi_major AND abi_minor <= host.abi_minor. api_use is a DECLARED-API-USE bitmask — diagnostics/compatibility only, NEVER a sandbox (a native plugin is arbitrary in-process code and the docs say so). A NULL lifecycle callback pointer = 'not interested'.

api_use.note: Declared API use (design 6 / review finding 14): a self-declared compatibility hint set, validated only as a subset sanity check, NEVER enforced as a sandbox.
